title: Agent Raw Definition
description: Authored agent definition as it arrives. Entry point to the pipeline DAG. Mostly written by an agent rather than by hand, which is why incorrect input is blocked and returned here rather than repaired downstream. Paths are workspace-relative, includes are file references, no computed sections.

indirect.title: Indirect
indirect.description: System-facing metadata and dispatcher configuration. Nothing here appears in the agent prompt.

metadata.title: Metadata
metadata.description: Agent identity. agent_name becomes the system identifier. agent_description is the one-line purpose statement.

agent_name.title: AgentName
agent_name.description:
Kebab-case identifier for the agent. Becomes the frontmatter `name` field in the generated agent prompt. Must be unique across all agent definitions. Use descriptive names that communicate domain and function: truth-system- quality-control, not qc-agent.
Lowercase kebab-case string — words separated by hyphens. Used for identifiers that must be URL-safe and filesystem-safe.

agent_description.title: AgentDescription
agent_description.description:
One-line purpose statement for the agent. Becomes the frontmatter `description` field in the generated agent prompt. Should complete the sentence "This agent..." without starting with "This agent". Be specific about what the agent does, not what it is. "Assesses truth entries against quality dimensions" not "A quality control agent".
Substantive prose text that forms complete sentences. Starts with a capital letter, contains at least three whitespace characters, ends with sentence punctuation. Structural constraints prevent non-prose abuse, so path exclusions are not needed. Used for descriptions, instructions, and multi-sentence text that may reference file paths.

x-semantic.intent: Communicates the agent's purpose to humans and systems that select agents for tasks. Vague descriptions make agents undiscoverable.
checks: Completes the sentence 'This agent...' naturally
Describes what the agent does, not what it is
Specific enough to distinguish from other agents
anti_patterns: Starting with 'This agent' or 'An agent that'
Describing identity instead of action: 'A quality control agent'

semantic_version.title: SemanticVersion
semantic_version.description:
Semantic version string in MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH format. Increment major for breaking changes, minor for new capabilities, patch for fixes.
Semantic version in MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH format. Increment major for breaking changes, minor for new capabilities, patch for fixes.

dispatch.title: Dispatch
dispatch.description: Dispatcher configuration — batching, concurrency, execution mode, and data flow.

dispatch_mode.title: DispatchMode
dispatch_mode.description:
How the dispatcher feeds work to the agent. 'batch' means the dispatcher splits input into chunks and invokes the agent once per chunk — requires dispatch_batch_size. 'full' means the dispatcher passes all input at once in a single agent invocation.
How the dispatcher feeds work to the agent. 'batch' splits input into chunks and invokes the agent once per chunk — requires dispatch_batch_size. 'full' passes all input at once in a single agent invocation.

dispatch_background_mode.title: DispatchBackgroundMode
dispatch_background_mode.description:
Background execution policy for this agent. Determines how the dispatcher handles this agent's execution lifecycle. 'allowed' means the dispatcher chooses foreground or background based on workload — most common choice. 'required' means the dispatcher must launch this agent as a background process — use for long-running agents that should not block the dispatcher. 'forbidden' means the agent must run in the foreground and the dispatcher waits for completion — use for interactive agents requiring user input.
Background execution policy. 'allowed' means the dispatcher chooses foreground or background based on workload. 'required' means the agent must run as a background process. 'forbidden' means the agent must run in the foreground and the dispatcher waits for completion.

dispatch_input_format.title: DispatchInputFormat
dispatch_input_format.description:
Format of the input data the agent receives. 'jsonl' for newline-delimited JSON records (one per line). 'json' for a single JSON document. 'text' for unstructured text content. This determines how the agent should parse the input file delivered via the delivery mechanism.
Format of input file content. 'jsonl' for newline-delimited JSON records, 'json' for a single JSON document, 'text' for unstructured text.

dispatch_input_delivery.title: DispatchInputDelivery
dispatch_input_delivery.description:
How input data reaches the agent. 'file' means the agent reads from a pre- determined file path declared in the definition — also requires security_io_input_file in [security.security_io]. 'directory' means the agent reads from a pre-determined directory path — also requires security_io_input_directory in [security.security_io]. 'tempfile' means the dispatcher writes input to a scoped temp directory and passes the path as parameter — preserves context window for large inputs; also requires security_io_input_tempdir in [security.security_io]. 'inline' means embedded directly in the agent prompt (small inputs only, no file paths or security_io fields needed).
How input data reaches the agent. 'tempfile' means the dispatcher writes to a scoped temp directory and passes the path as parameter. 'inline' means embedded directly in the agent prompt. 'file' means the agent reads from a pre-determined file path. 'directory' means the agent reads from a pre-determined directory path.

dispatch_input_description.title: DispatchInputDescription
dispatch_input_description.description:
Human-readable description of the input data the agent receives. Describes what the records represent and what the agent does with them. The mechanical format is captured by dispatch_input_format and delivery by dispatch_input_delivery — this field captures domain meaning, but repeating format for human readability is acceptable. Example: "Embedding target records to rewrite and compress to 80-150 characters"
Natural language prose — must contain at least one whitespace character. Mutually exclusive with all identifier types. Used for descriptions, instructions, error messages, and display labels. Not a path.

dispatch_max_agents.title: DispatchMaxAgents
dispatch_max_agents.description:
Maximum number of concurrent agent instances the dispatcher may spawn. Controls parallelism for batch processing. The dispatcher launches up to this many agents simultaneously, each processing a different chunk. Defaults to 6 if not specified.
Whole number value

dispatch_batch_size.title: DispatchBatchSize
dispatch_batch_size.description:
Tuple of [min, max] records per batch chunk. The dispatcher splits input into chunks of size between min and max. Min must be strictly less than max. Required when dispatch_mode is 'batch'. Example: [50, 100] means each agent invocation gets between 50 and 100 records.
[min, max] records per batch chunk. Min must be strictly less than max. The dispatcher splits input into chunks of size between min and max.

dispatch_parameters.title: DispatchParameters
dispatch_parameters.description: Named parameters the dispatcher passes to the agent at invocation

items.title: ParameterItem
items.description: A parameter the dispatcher passes to the agent at invocation

param_name.title: ParamName
param_name.description:
Name of a parameter the dispatcher passes to the agent. This becomes the placeholder name in the agent prompt template. Common names: 'tempfile' (path to input data), 'uid' (record identifier), 'iteration' (processing round number).
Lowercase snake_case string — words separated by underscores. Used for parameter names and template placeholders.

param_type.title: ParamType
param_type.description:
Type of the parameter value. Used for documentation and dispatcher validation. 'path' for filesystem paths, 'string' for arbitrary text, 'integer' for numeric values, 'boolean' for true/false flags.
Type of a dispatch parameter value. Used for documentation and dispatcher validation.

param_required.title: ParamRequired
param_required.description:
Whether this parameter must be provided by the dispatcher. Required parameters cause dispatcher failure if missing. Optional parameters have sensible defaults or conditional behavior.
True or false value

param_description.title: ParamDescription
param_description.description:
Human-readable description of what a dispatcher parameter represents and how the agent should interpret it. Optional — parameter name and type may be sufficient for self-documenting parameters.
Natural language prose — must contain at least one whitespace character. Mutually exclusive with all identifier types. Used for descriptions, instructions, error messages, and display labels. Not a path.

task.title: Task
task.description: Agent-facing identity and interaction model — paths absolutized

role.title: Role
role.description: Agent persona — identity and responsibility are required

role_identity.title: RoleIdentity
role_identity.description:
Short noun phrase naming what this agent is. Not a sentence, not a role description — that belongs in role and capabilities. Examples: "semantic quality assessor", "interview summarizer", "embedding normalizer". This becomes the "You are a {identity}" opening in the generated prompt.
Natural language prose — must contain at least one whitespace character. Mutually exclusive with all identifier types. Used for descriptions, instructions, error messages, and display labels. Not a path.

x-semantic.intent: Establishes the agent's behavioral frame. The generated prompt opens "You are a {role_identity}" — vague identities produce vague behavior.
checks: Specific enough to distinguish this agent from others in the system
Noun phrase, not a sentence or role description
Names a recognizable specialist, not a generic label
anti_patterns: Sentences or descriptions instead of noun phrases

role_responsibility.title: RoleResponsibility
role_responsibility.description:
One-sentence mandate defining the agent's core obligation. This is the single most important thing the agent must accomplish. Everything else is secondary. Write as a direct imperative: "Assess each truth entry against quality dimensions and produce a structured QC report."
Substantive prose text that forms complete sentences. Starts with a capital letter, contains at least three whitespace characters, ends with sentence punctuation. Structural constraints prevent non-prose abuse, so path exclusions are not needed. Used for descriptions, instructions, and multi-sentence text that may reference file paths.

x-semantic.intent: Defines the agent's primary obligation. Everything else the agent does is secondary to this. A weak responsibility produces unfocused execution.
checks: Single clear mandate, not a list of duties
Written as direct imperative
Specific enough that completion is verifiable
Describes an outcome, not an activity
anti_patterns: Describing what the agent IS instead of what it MUST DO

role_description.title: RoleDescription
role_description.description:
Expanded role context that builds on role_identity and role_responsibility. Where identity says WHAT you are and responsibility says WHAT you must do, description provides the WHY and HOW — domain context, judgement guidance, and framing that shapes how the agent approaches its work. Optional for simple agents; increasingly valuable as task complexity and required judgement increase.
Substantive prose text that forms complete sentences. Starts with a capital letter, contains at least three whitespace characters, ends with sentence punctuation. Structural constraints prevent non-prose abuse, so path exclusions are not needed. Used for descriptions, instructions, and multi-sentence text that may reference file paths.

x-semantic.intent: Builds the agent's understanding of its role beyond the identity and responsibility. Provides context, nuance, and framing that helps the agent exercise good judgement in ambiguous situations.
checks: Adds context beyond what identity and responsibility already state
Helps the agent understand WHY it does what it does
Appropriate depth for task complexity — simple agents may omit entirely
anti_patterns: Restating role_identity or role_responsibility in different words
Generic filler: 'You are a helpful assistant that...'

items.title: RoleExpertiseItem
items.description:
Skill and knowledge areas the agent claims. Each entry is a concise phrase describing a competency relevant to the agent's task. These calibrate the LLM's self-model — declare expertise areas that directly support role_responsibility. Typical agents declare 2-5 entries. Be specific: "JSON Schema validation" not "validation", "Gothic linguistic terminology" not "languages". If provided, must contain at least one entry (omit the field entirely rather than providing an empty array). Entries must be unique.
Natural language prose — must contain at least one whitespace character. Mutually exclusive with all identifier types. Used for descriptions, instructions, error messages, and display labels. Not a path.

return.title: Return
return.description: How the agent returns results. return_mode drives which instruction fields the format transformer composes into the prompt. Path absolutized after resolution.

return_mode.title: ReturnMode
return_mode.description:
How the agent returns results to the dispatcher. status: return only SUCCESS or FAILURE. status-metrics: return status plus summary metrics. metrics- output: return metrics plus actual output data. output: return output directly, no status word needed. Determines which return instructions the format transformer composes into the prompt.
How the agent returns results. 'status' returns only SUCCESS or FAILURE. 'status-metrics' returns status plus summary metrics. 'metrics-output' returns metrics plus actual output data. 'output' returns output directly with no status word.

return_status.title: ReturnStatus
return_status.description:
Prompt instruction for the status portion of the agent return. Composed into the prompt when return_mode includes status (status or status- metrics). Authors may customize to include agent-specific success criteria.
Substantive prose text that forms complete sentences. Starts with a capital letter, contains at least three whitespace characters, ends with sentence punctuation. Structural constraints prevent non-prose abuse, so path exclusions are not needed. Used for descriptions, instructions, and multi-sentence text that may reference file paths.
return_status.default: Return only SUCCESS or FAILURE. SUCCESS means the process completed correctly regardless of data outcomes. FAILURE means the process itself broke.

return_metrics.title: ReturnMetrics
return_metrics.description:
Prompt instruction for the metrics portion of the agent return. Composed into the prompt when return_mode includes metrics (status-metrics or metrics-output). Authors may customize to specify agent-specific metrics.
Substantive prose text that forms complete sentences. Starts with a capital letter, contains at least three whitespace characters, ends with sentence punctuation. Structural constraints prevent non-prose abuse, so path exclusions are not needed. Used for descriptions, instructions, and multi-sentence text that may reference file paths.
return_metrics.default: Include summary metrics with your return: records processed, records passed, records failed.

return_output.title: ReturnOutput
return_output.description:
Prompt instruction for the output portion of the agent return. Composed into the prompt when return_mode includes output (metrics-output or output). Authors may customize to specify agent-specific output instructions.
Substantive prose text that forms complete sentences. Starts with a capital letter, contains at least three whitespace characters, ends with sentence punctuation. Structural constraints prevent non-prose abuse, so path exclusions are not needed. Used for descriptions, instructions, and multi-sentence text that may reference file paths.
return_output.default: Return your output directly as your final message to the dispatcher.

processing.title: Processing
processing.description: Output processing configuration — file format, naming, write frequency, model capability tier, and scratch space needs.

capability_model.title: AgentCapabilityModel
capability_model.description:
Platform-agnostic capability tier for this agent. Format transformers map descriptors to vendor-specific models. fast-cheap: speed/cost over quality (bulk transforms, simple extraction). standard: general-purpose balance. analytical: careful judgment (QC, assessment, structured analysis). complex- reasoning: deep multi-step reasoning (text rewriting, nuanced decisions). max-capability: highest available, no compromises. inherit: match the dispatcher's model (task scales with calling context).
Platform-agnostic capability tier. Format transformers map to vendor models. 'fast-cheap' for bulk transforms. 'standard' for general purpose. 'analytical' for careful judgment. 'complex-reasoning' for deep multi-step reasoning. 'max-capability' for highest available. 'inherit' to match the dispatcher's model.

output_description.title: OutputDescription
output_description.description:
Human-readable description of the output data the agent produces. Describes what the output contains and its downstream purpose. The mechanical format is captured by processing_output_file_format — this field captures domain meaning, but repeating format for human readability is acceptable. Example: "One assessment record per input entry with quality scores and failure annotations"
Natural language prose — must contain at least one whitespace character. Mutually exclusive with all identifier types. Used for descriptions, instructions, error messages, and display labels. Not a path.

scratch_needed.title: ScratchNeeded
scratch_needed.description:
Whether this agent needs a scratch directory for intermediate files. When true, security_io_scratch_tempdir must be provided and the agent auto- derives write access to a scoped temp path. Off by default — most agents keep intermediate state in context. Enable when an agent processes sequential data that loses coherence without file-based checkpointing, or when LLM behavior requires scratch space for processing optimization.
True or false value

output_file_format.title: OutputFileFormat
output_file_format.description:
The output format the agent produces. Determines file extension enforcement and format validation hooks. JSONL enables record-level write frequency control via processing_output_write_frequency.
Output format the agent produces. 'jsonl' for record-oriented output, 'json' for a single structured document, 'markdown' for prose or structured text with headings, 'text' for unstructured plain text.

output_file_name_known.title: OutputFileNameKnown
output_file_name_known.description:
How well the output filename is known at definition time. known: exact output file path is declared — also requires security_io_output_file in [security.security_io]. partially: a naming template or instruction constrains the filename but the LLM provides variable parts — also requires security_io_output_directory in [security.security_io], plus processing_output_file_name_template. unknown: completely dynamic, no naming constraint — also requires security_io_output_directory in [security.security_io], plus processing_output_file_name_instruction.
How well the output filename is known at definition time. 'known' means exact path is declared. 'partially' means a naming template constrains the filename. 'unknown' means completely dynamic naming.

output_file_name_template.title: OutputFileNameTemplate
output_file_name_template.description:
Filename template with {placeholder} syntax for dispatch-time parameters. The tool constructs the output filename by substituting placeholder values provided by the LLM (received as dispatch parameters). The tool controls directory, naming pattern, and extension. The LLM controls only the variable parts. Example: "{interview-id}.summaries.jsonl" — the LLM provides interview-id, the tool constructs the full path.
Filename template with a {variable} placeholder and file extension. The variable becomes the --name CLI argument for the output tool. The extension segments determine the output file suffix. LLM authors write the complete template; the build system decomposes it into tool arguments and write paths.

output_file_name_instruction.title: OutputFileNameInstruction
output_file_name_instruction.description:
Instruction indicating what the LLM should use as the filename basis during processing. The LLM derives the identifier from the data being processed. The tool writes to output_directory/{identifier}.{extension}, where the extension is enforced by processing_output_file_format. The LLM controls the filename but not the directory or file type. Example: "{record-identifier}" — the LLM provides a record identifier, the tool writes to the output directory with the correct extension.
Substantive prose text that forms complete sentences. Starts with a capital letter, contains at least three whitespace characters, ends with sentence punctuation. Structural constraints prevent non-prose abuse, so path exclusions are not needed. Used for descriptions, instructions, and multi-sentence text that may reference file paths.

output_write_frequency.title: OutputWriteFrequency
output_write_frequency.description:
How often the agent flushes records to disk. record: one record per write invocation, minimal blast radius. batch: bounded set of records per invocation, size controlled by processing_output_batch_size. Only relevant for JSONL — other formats write the entire file per invocation by default.
How often records are flushed to disk. 'record' means one record per write invocation with minimal blast radius. 'batch' means a bounded set of records per invocation with size controlled by batch_size.

output_batch_size.title: OutputBatchSize
output_batch_size.description:
Number of records per write tool call when write frequency is batch. The agent accumulates this many records before invoking the write tool. Balances write frequency against data loss risk from interruption.
Whole number value

notify.title: Notify
notify.description: Notification rules — when to trigger, what to say, how to deliver

items.title: NotifyItem
items.description: A notification rule — when to trigger, what to say, how to deliver

notify_trigger.title: NotifyTrigger
notify_trigger.description:
When to trigger an agent-initiated notification. A human-readable condition the agent evaluates during processing. "every 100 records processed", "on first schema validation failure", "when processing completes". The transformer compiles this into echo instructions in the processing section.
Natural language prose — must contain at least one whitespace character. Mutually exclusive with all identifier types. Used for descriptions, instructions, error messages, and display labels. Not a path.

notify_message.title: NotifyMessage
notify_message.description:
Message template for agent-initiated notifications. Can contain {placeholders} the agent fills in at runtime. "{n} of {total} processed, {remaining} remaining". The agent echoes this with a ::notify:: prefix; the hook intercepts and routes to the delivery mechanism.
Natural language prose — must contain at least one whitespace character. Mutually exclusive with all identifier types. Used for descriptions, instructions, error messages, and display labels. Not a path.

notify_delivery.title: NotifyDelivery
notify_delivery.description:
How to deliver agent-initiated notifications. 'say' uses macOS text-to- speech (good for background monitoring). 'notification' uses macOS Notification Center via osascript (urgent alerts). 'terminal' rings the bell and prints the message. 'log' writes silently to a log file.
How to deliver agent-initiated notifications. 'say' uses macOS text-to-speech. 'notification' uses macOS Notification Center. 'terminal' rings the bell and prints. 'log' writes silently to a log file.

security.title: Security
security.description: Access control — tools, paths, capabilities, context resources. Everything needed for computing minimum privileges.

security_io.title: SecurityIo
security_io.description: Concrete I/O targets. Input side auto-grants read permission. Output side produces the enforcement output tool — not a generic write permission.

io_input_file.title: IoInputFileAny
io_input_file.description:
Workspace-relative path to the input file. Automatically grants read tool and read permission to this file — no need to also list it in security_paths_allowed_read. Validated against the path blocklist. Example: "interview/data/input.jsonl"
Filesystem path — either relative (./) or absolute (/)

io_input_directory.title: IoInputDirectoryAny
io_input_directory.description:
Workspace-relative path to the input directory. Automatically grants read tool and read permission to all files within this directory — no need to also list it in security_paths_allowed_read. Validated against the path blocklist. Example: "interview/data/"
Filesystem path — either relative (./) or absolute (/)

io_input_tempdir.title: IoInputTempdir
io_input_tempdir.description:
Opaque directory name (a short slug, not a path) for this agent type's temp staging area. The dispatcher writes input data to /tmp/{workspace}/{value}/ and the agent auto-derives read access to that scoped path. Provide only the name segment — e.g., "cobalt-stage", not "/tmp/myworkspace/cobalt-stage". The format transformer may hash both workspace and value for obfuscation on disk. Must not be derived from the agent name or reveal agent structure — if names follow a predictable pattern, an adversarial LLM can enumerate temp directories for other agent types. Choose an arbitrary, non-descriptive name per agent type. Examples: "cobalt-stage", "theta-7" (good); "embedding- normalizer-input", "input" (bad — reveals agent identity or is too predictable).
Lowercase kebab-case string — words separated by hyphens. Used for identifiers that must be URL-safe and filesystem-safe.

constraints.reason: Input tempdir (read access) and scratch tempdir (write access) must not resolve to the same path. Same value would give the agent write access to its input staging area.

io_scratch_tempdir.title: IoScratchTempdir
io_scratch_tempdir.description:
Opaque directory name (a short slug, not a path) for this agent type's scratch/intermediate file area. The agent auto-derives write access to /tmp/{workspace}/{value}/ for intermediate processing files. Provide only the name segment — e.g., "cedar-scratch", not "/tmp/myworkspace/cedar- scratch". The format transformer may hash both workspace and value for obfuscation on disk. Same opaque naming rules as security_io_input_tempdir — must not be derived from the agent name or reveal agent structure. Examples: "cedar-scratch", "work-bravo" (good); "my-agent-work" (bad — reveals agent identity).
Lowercase kebab-case string — words separated by hyphens. Used for identifiers that must be URL-safe and filesystem-safe.

constraints.reason: Input tempdir (read access) and scratch tempdir (write access) must not resolve to the same path. Same value would give the agent write access to its input staging area, defeating isolation between dispatcher- written input and agent-written scratch files.
Scratch tempdir must not overlap with the output directory. Same path would allow unconstrained scratch writes to masquerade as validated output.

io_output_file.title: IoOutputFileAny
io_output_file.description:
Workspace-relative path to the agent's output file. The security resolver uses this path to create a constrained write tool that enforces schema validation, format checking, and batch size limits on every write. This path must NOT appear in security_paths_allowed_write — if it did, the agent would have a second, unconstrained write path bypassing all enforcement. Validated against the path blocklist. Example: "interview/output/results.jsonl"
Filesystem path — either relative (./) or absolute (/)

constraints.reason: Output path in the write fence defeats bound tool constraints. The agent would have generic write access via platform tools, bypassing schema validation, format enforcement, and batch limits.
Output path identical to a write fence path defeats bound tool constraints. The agent would have generic write access to the same location, bypassing schema validation and format enforcement.

io_output_directory.title: IoOutputDirectoryAny
io_output_directory.description:
Workspace-relative path to the agent's output directory. The security resolver uses this to create a constrained write tool that enforces schema validation, format checking, and batch size limits on every write within this directory. This path must NOT appear in security_paths_allowed_write — if it did, the agent would have unconstrained write access bypassing all enforcement. Validated against the path blocklist. Example: "interview/output/"
Filesystem path — either relative (./) or absolute (/)

constraints.reason: Output path in the write fence defeats bound tool constraints. The agent would have generic write access via platform tools, bypassing schema validation, format enforcement, and batch limits.
Output path identical to a write fence path defeats bound tool constraints. The agent would have generic write access to the same location, bypassing schema validation and format enforcement.

security_schema.title: SecuritySchema
security_schema.description: Data schema declarations for input and output. Schema validation enforcement is a security property.

input_schema.title: InputSchemaXAny
input_schema.description:
Schema the input data validates against. Workspace-relative path to a .schema.json or .schema.yaml file. When provided, the resolver uses this for input validation enforcement before the agent processes data — a security property that catches malformed input early. Optional: include when the agent's input has a defined schema and you want pre-validation. Omit when input is unstructured text or when input validation is handled upstream. Schema file must exist at resolution time.
Filesystem path that must exist — either relative or absolute

output_schema.title: OutputSchemaXAny
output_schema.description:
Schema the output data must validate against. Workspace-relative path to a .schema.json or .schema.yaml file. Required when the agent produces structured output (JSON or JSONL) — the enforcement output tool uses this schema to validate records before writing. Optional for unstructured output (markdown, text) where schema validation is not applicable. Lives in the security section because the resolver needs it for engineering control derivation — schema validation is a security enforcement property. Schema file must exist at resolution time.
Filesystem path that must exist — either relative or absolute

constraints.reason: Structured output (JSON or JSONL) requires a schema for validation enforcement. Without a schema, the enforcement output tool cannot validate records before writing.

return_schema.title: ReturnSchemaXAny
return_schema.description:
Workspace-relative path to a JSON Schema file (must end with .schema.json or .schema.yaml) defining the metric fields the agent returns. Always embedded directly into the prompt — there is no enforcement mechanism for return communication (agent-to-dispatcher LLM text). Embedding ensures the agent sees field names, types, and definitions. Schema file must exist at resolution time. Example: "definitions/schemas/my-agent-return.schema.json"
Filesystem path that must exist — either relative or absolute

output_schema_embed.title: OutputSchemaEmbed
output_schema_embed.description:
Whether to embed the output schema directly into the agent prompt. Authored here, in the data — the decision is made before rendering, not by a control surface. When true, the schema's content is inlined and the read grant is suppressed: the agent sees the schema with no tool call. When false (or omitted), the schema path is granted read access and the agent reads it via the Read tool — one round trip, and the content arrives as a recent turn. Prefer true for small schemas (under ~100 lines) or when adherence is critical. Prefer false for large ones — the cost is not only context window: a large inlined block lands mid-prompt where attention is weakest, and pushes every later section further into that same trough. There is no free position for it. Which way is better for a given schema is worth building both ways and testing. Either way the agent knows the desired shape.
True or false value

security_paths.title: SecurityPaths
security_paths.description: Filesystem path grants at two permission levels. At least one path grant must be present. Read-level enables read, search, inspect. Write-level enables all capabilities.

paths_workspace.title: WorkspacePathXAbs
paths_workspace.description:
Absolute filesystem path to the workspace root directory. All workspace- relative paths in the definition (context paths, schema paths, allowed_read/write paths) are resolved relative to this directory. Must be an absolute path (starting with /). Validated against the blocklist during resolution. Any path that resolves outside this workspace or into a blocked zone triggers a SecurityIncident. Example: "/Users/username/ai/spaces/myproject"
Absolute path that must exist on the filesystem

paths_allowed_read.title: PathsAllowedRead
paths_allowed_read.description: MOST AGENTS DO NOT NEED THIS — read access is auto-derived from security_io, security_schema, and context declarations. Only add paths here for workspace locations NOT covered by those declarations.

items.title: PathsAllowedReadAny
items.description:
WARNING — MOST AGENTS DO NOT NEED THIS. Read permissions for input files, context resources, schemas, and temp directories are ALL AUTO-DERIVED from their respective declarations. Adding them here is REDUNDANT and indicates a misunderstanding of the security model. THIS IS ONLY FOR additional workspace paths the agent reads that are NOT declared anywhere else — e.g., reference data directories, shared configuration files, library sources. If every path you want to add here is already declared in security_io, security_schema, or context, LEAVE THIS EMPTY. Each entry grants recursive read-level access to all files under the prefix. Entries can be workspace- relative or absolute. Actual capabilities granted depend on intersection with security_capabilities_requested.
Filesystem path — either relative (./) or absolute (/)

paths_allowed_write.title: PathsAllowedWrite
paths_allowed_write.description: MOST AGENTS DO NOT NEED THIS — write access is auto-derived from security_io declarations. NEVER put output paths here — that bypasses enforcement. Only add paths here for workspace locations NOT covered by security_io.

items.title: PathsAllowedWriteAny
items.description:
WARNING — MOST AGENTS DO NOT NEED THIS. Write permissions for output files, output directories, temp dirs, and scratch dirs are ALL AUTO-DERIVED from security_io declarations. NEVER put output paths here — doing so BYPASSES schema validation, format enforcement, and batch size limits that the enforcement output tool enforces. THIS IS ONLY FOR workspace paths where the agent needs UNCONSTRAINED write access to locations NOT declared in security_io — e.g., updating shared state files, writing logs to a common directory. If every path you want to add here is already declared in security_io, LEAVE THIS EMPTY. Each entry grants recursive write-level access (write, edit, append, plus read, search, inspect) to all files under the prefix. Entries can be workspace-relative or absolute.
Filesystem path — either relative (./) or absolute (/)

context.title: Context
context.description: Resources the agent needs access to — auto-derives read permissions

context_required.title: ContextRequired
context_required.description: Context the agent MUST use. An instruction, not a listing: the agent is required to utilize these resources and to abort rather than proceed without them. Contrast context_available, which only informs the agent that further material exists. The two must stay distinct all the way to the rendered prompt — they exist so the prompt can carry must-language and should-language as visibly different prose. Paths are absolutized during the build.

context_available.title: ContextAvailable
context_available.description: Context the agent MAY use — information that further material exists and is reachable. The agent is not required to consult it. Contrast context_required, which is a mandatory instruction the agent must satisfy or abort. The two must stay distinct all the way to the rendered prompt — they exist so the prompt can carry should-language and must-language as visibly different prose. Paths are absolutized during the build.

capabilities_requested.title: CapabilitiesRequested
capabilities_requested.description: Platform-agnostic capabilities the agent requests. A requested capability is only granted if a matching path grant exists and it is not prohibited.

items.title: CapabilitiesRequested
items.description:
WARNING — MOST AGENTS SHOULD LEAVE THIS EMPTY. Capabilities for input files, output files, context resources, schemas, temp dirs, and scratch dirs are ALL AUTO-DERIVED by the security resolver. You do NOT need to request read for input files or write for output files — that happens automatically from security_io declarations. THIS IS ONLY FOR capabilities the agent needs on EXPLICIT path grants (security_paths_allowed_read and security_paths_allowed_write). If the agent has no explicit path grants, this array MUST be empty. Each entry is a platform-agnostic capability descriptor, not a vendor tool name. A requested capability is only granted if a matching explicit path grant exists and the capability is not prohibited. Format transformers map capability names to vendor-specific tools.
Platform-agnostic capability descriptor. Format transformers map these to vendor-specific tools. read: file read. search: find files by name or content. write: create or overwrite files. edit: targeted modification. append: add content to end of files. inspect: read-only command execution.

capabilities_prohibited.title: CapabilitiesProhibited
capabilities_prohibited.description: Capabilities to deny even if path grants exist. Takes precedence over both explicit path grants and auto-derived permissions.

items.title: CapabilitiesProhibited
items.description:
Platform-agnostic capabilities to deny even if path grants exist. Each entry is a capability descriptor, not a vendor tool name. Takes precedence over both explicit path grants and auto-derived permissions. Format transformers map capability names to vendor-specific tools.

execution.title: Execution
execution.description: How the agent processes work — instructions and examples

execution_instructions.title: ExecutionInstructions
execution_instructions.description: Ordered processing steps — inline or included from .md files

oneOf.title: InstructionStep
oneOf.description: Inline instruction step with processing mode boundary

instruction_mode.title: InstructionMode
instruction_mode.description:
Processing mode boundary. DETERMINISTIC steps are mechanical operations (reading input, writing output, validating schema) where the LLM must follow exact procedures with no creativity. PROBABILISTIC steps require LLM intelligence (rewriting text, making quality judgments, creative decisions). The transformer uses mode declarations to compile different prompt patterns for each step type.
Processing mode boundary. 'deterministic' steps are mechanical operations where the LLM must follow exact procedures. 'probabilistic' steps require LLM intelligence for creative or evaluative work.

instruction_text.title: InstructionText
instruction_text.description:
Inline instruction text for this step. Used for short instructions that don't warrant a separate .md file. Mutually exclusive with include.
Markdown-formatted text content. Starts with a non-path character, contains at least three whitespace characters. No path exclusions needed — the structural constraints prevent abuse while allowing markdown formatting and embedded path references. Used for example content, instructional text, and rich-text fields.

x-semantic.intent: Directs agent behavior for one processing step. Each instruction must produce consistent behavior across different LLM instances.
checks: Specific enough that two different LLMs would produce similar outputs
Describes concrete actions, not aspirational goals
Scoped to a single processing step, not the entire task

oneOf.title: IncludeInstruction
oneOf.description: @path reference to a .md file that expands to instruction steps. Resolver splits at H2 boundaries and derives instruction_mode from headings.

include.title: IncludeInstructionXAny
include.description:
An @path reference to a .md file that expands to one or many instruction steps. The resolver reads the file, splits at H2 boundaries, and derives instruction_mode from each H2 heading.
Filesystem path that must exist — either relative or absolute

execution_examples.title: ExecutionExamples
execution_examples.description: Example groups with entries — inline or included from .md files

oneOf.title: ExampleGroup
oneOf.description: A named group of calibration examples with optional heading display and count limits

example_group_name.title: ExampleGroupName
example_group_name.description:
Name of the example group, used as the H3 heading when compiling examples into the agent prompt. Groups organize examples by what they demonstrate — "correct rewrite", "incorrect compression", "edge cases".
Title Case string — each word starts uppercase, separated by spaces. Used for display titles, section headings, and short labels. Not prose (no sentences), not an identifier (has spaces).

example_display_headings.title: ExampleDisplayHeadings
example_display_headings.description:
Toggle per-group display of individual example headings. When false, examples render as items under the group H3. When true, each example gets its own H4 heading derived from the H2 in the resolved content. Controls detail level without changing content.
True or false value

examples_max_number.title: ExamplesMaxNumber
examples_max_number.description:
Maximum number of examples to include from this group after include resolution and H2 splitting. Applied AFTER the transformer resolves @include references and splits on H2 boundaries — the count is about resolved individual examples, not raw array entries. Omit to include all examples in the group.
Whole number value

example_entries.title: ExampleEntries
example_entries.description: Example entries — inline or included from .md files

oneOf.title: ExampleEntry
oneOf.description: Inline example with heading and text content

example_heading.title: ExampleHeading
example_heading.description:
Heading for an individual example entry. When example_display_headings is true, this becomes the H4 heading for the example in the generated prompt. When derived from @include, the resolver extracts this from the H2 heading in the source .md file.
Natural language prose — must contain at least one whitespace character. Mutually exclusive with all identifier types. Used for descriptions, instructions, error messages, and display labels. Not a path.

example_text.title: ExampleText
example_text.description:
Inline example text for this entry. Used for short examples that don't warrant a separate .md file. Mutually exclusive with include.

No path exclusions needed — the structural constraints prevent abuse while allowing markdown formatting and embedded path references. Used for example content, instructional text, and rich-text fields.

oneOf.title: IncludeExample
oneOf.description: @path reference to a .md file that expands to example entries. Resolver splits at H2 boundaries and derives example_heading from headings.

include.title: IncludeExampleXAny
include.description:
An @path reference to a .md file that expands to one or many example entries. The resolver reads the file, splits at H2 boundaries, and derives example_heading from each H2.
Filesystem path that must exist — either relative or absolute

oneOf.title: IncludeExampleGroup
oneOf.description: @path reference to a .md file that expands to a complete example group. Resolver derives group name, entries, and headings from file structure.

include.title: IncludeExampleGroupXAny
include.description:

criteria.title: Criteria
criteria.description: Quality criteria — guardrails, success conditions, failure conditions. At least one must be present.

guardrails.title: Guardrails
guardrails.description: Behavioral constraints and known failure patterns — at least one must be present

guardrails_constraints.title: GuardrailsConstraints
guardrails_constraints.description: MUST and NEVER rules the agent must follow. Each entry is a single imperative constraint. Keep constraints specific and verifiable.

items.title: GuardrailsConstraint
items.description:
MUST and NEVER rules the agent must follow. Each entry is a single imperative constraint. "MUST validate every record against schema before writing", "NEVER modify source data", "MUST process records in order". Keep constraints specific and verifiable — vague rules get ignored.
Substantive prose text that forms complete sentences. Starts with a capital letter, contains at least three whitespace characters, ends with sentence punctuation. Structural constraints prevent non-prose abuse, so path exclusions are not needed. Used for descriptions, instructions, and multi-sentence text that may reference file paths.

x-semantic.intent: Hard behavioral boundaries in the agent prompt. Violations are agent failures. Each item must be clear enough that both the agent AND a reviewer can determine whether a specific output violates it.
checks: Each item is actionable — agent can determine compliance from the constraint alone
Each item is verifiable — a reviewer can check violation without ambiguity
Items are specific to this agent's failure modes, not generic good practice
anti_patterns: Constraints the agent cannot actually verify or enforce

guardrails_anti_patterns.title: GuardrailsAntiPatterns
guardrails_anti_patterns.description: Common mistakes to avoid. Each entry describes a specific wrong behavior the agent might exhibit and why it's wrong.

items.title: GuardrailsAntiPattern
items.description:
Common mistakes to avoid. Each entry describes a specific wrong behavior the agent might exhibit and why it's wrong. "Do not batch-summarize from memory — process each record individually from the source file", "Do not infer missing fields — mark them as absent". Anti-patterns are learned from observed agent failures.
Substantive prose text that forms complete sentences. Starts with a capital letter, contains at least three whitespace characters, ends with sentence punctuation. Structural constraints prevent non-prose abuse, so path exclusions are not needed. Used for descriptions, instructions, and multi-sentence text that may reference file paths.

x-semantic.intent: Calibrates the LLM against its own failure modes. Each item must describe a specific, recognizable mistake — not a generic warning.
checks: Each item describes a specific mistake, not a category of mistakes
Each item is recognizable — agent can detect when it is about to do this
Items are grounded in observed LLM failure modes, not hypothetical risks

include_guardrails_constraints.title: IncludeGuardrailsConstraints
include_guardrails_constraints.description: @path reference to a .md file containing constraints

include.title: IncludeGuardrailsConstraintsXAny
include.description:
An @path reference to a .md file containing constraints. The resolver reads the file and extracts individual constraint items from its structure.
Filesystem path that must exist — either relative or absolute

include_guardrails_anti_patterns.title: IncludeGuardrailsAntiPatterns
include_guardrails_anti_patterns.description: @path reference to a .md file containing anti-patterns

include.title: IncludeGuardrailsAntiPatternsXAny
include.description:

Filesystem path that must exist — either relative or absolute

success_criteria.title: SuccessCriteria
success_criteria.description: Success criteria — inline definitions or included from .md files

oneOf.title: SuccessItem
oneOf.description: A single success criterion with definition and observable evidence

success_definition.title: SuccessDefinition
success_definition.description:
One-sentence statement of what success means for this agent. LLMs are goal- driven — explicit success definitions pull harder than constraints. Write as a positive outcome: "Every input record has been assessed and a valid QC report written to disk."
Substantive prose text that forms complete sentences. Starts with a capital letter, contains at least three whitespace characters, ends with sentence punctuation. Structural constraints prevent non-prose abuse, so path exclusions are not needed. Used for descriptions, instructions, and multi-sentence text that may reference file paths.

x-semantic.intent: The agent's goal state. LLMs are goal-driven — explicit success definitions pull behavior more effectively than constraints push it.
checks: Describes a concrete end state, not an ongoing activity
Refers to the PROCESS succeeding, not data quality outcomes
Observable — you can tell from examining outputs whether this was achieved
anti_patterns: Confusing process success with data quality ('all entries are high quality' is data, not process)
Vague outcomes: 'task completed successfully', 'all items processed'

success_evidence.title: SuccessEvidence
success_evidence.description: Observable evidence that a success criterion has been met

items.title: SuccessEvidenceItem
items.description:
Observable conditions that prove success. Each entry is a concrete, verifiable statement the agent can check. "Output record count equals input record count", "Every record passes schema validation". These become the agent's self-verification checklist.
Substantive prose text that forms complete sentences. Starts with a capital letter, contains at least three whitespace characters, ends with sentence punctuation. Structural constraints prevent non-prose abuse, so path exclusions are not needed. Used for descriptions, instructions, and multi-sentence text that may reference file paths.

x-semantic.intent: Self-verification checklist. The agent checks each condition after processing to confirm success before reporting.
checks: Each item is a concrete, observable condition — not a subjective judgment
Each item is independently verifiable from outputs alone
Conditions are sufficient — if all pass, success is confirmed

oneOf.title: IncludeSuccessCriteria
oneOf.description: @path reference to a .md file containing success criteria

include.title: IncludeSuccessCriteriaXAny
include.description:
An @path reference to a .md file containing success criteria. The resolver reads the file and extracts individual success criterion items from its structure.
Filesystem path that must exist — either relative or absolute

failure_criteria.title: FailureCriteria
failure_criteria.description: Failure criteria — inline definitions or included from .md files

oneOf.title: FailureItem
oneOf.description: A single failure criterion — FAILURE means process broke, not data quality

failure_definition.title: FailureDefinition
failure_definition.description:
One-sentence statement of what failure means for this agent. Failure refers to the PROCESS, not the DATA. An agent that correctly identifies all inputs as invalid has SUCCEEDED — the assessment process worked. FAILURE means the process itself broke: couldn't read input, couldn't write output, unrecoverable error.
Substantive prose text that forms complete sentences. Starts with a capital letter, contains at least three whitespace characters, ends with sentence punctuation. Structural constraints prevent non-prose abuse, so path exclusions are not needed. Used for descriptions, instructions, and multi-sentence text that may reference file paths.

x-semantic.intent: Defines process failure — not data outcomes. The agent uses this to determine when to report FAILURE vs SUCCESS with bad-data findings.
checks: Describes PROCESS failure, not data quality problems
Specific failure conditions, not 'something went wrong'
Distinguishable from success_definition — no overlap
anti_patterns: Treating bad data as failure ('found invalid entries' is SUCCESS if the process worked)

failure_evidence.title: FailureEvidence
failure_evidence.description: Observable evidence that a failure criterion has been triggered

items.title: FailureEvidenceItem
items.description:
Observable conditions that prove failure. Each entry is a concrete condition indicating the process broke. "Any record skipped without explanation", "Schema validation failure not resolved after retry", "Output file not created". These are process failures, not data quality findings.
Substantive prose text that forms complete sentences. Starts with a capital letter, contains at least three whitespace characters, ends with sentence punctuation. Structural constraints prevent non-prose abuse, so path exclusions are not needed. Used for descriptions, instructions, and multi-sentence text that may reference file paths.

x-semantic.intent: Process failure detection. The agent checks these conditions to determine whether to report FAILURE instead of SUCCESS.
checks: Each item describes a PROCESS failure condition, not a data quality finding
Each item is observable from the execution environment
Conditions are distinct from success_evidence — no overlap

oneOf.title: IncludeFailureCriteria
oneOf.description: @path reference to a .md file containing failure criteria

include.title: IncludeFailureCriteriaXAny
include.description:
An @path reference to a .md file containing failure criteria. The resolver reads the file and extracts individual failure criterion items from its structure.
Filesystem path that must exist — either relative or absolute

pattern__relative.title: Relative
pattern__relative.description: Starts with dot — relative path prefix (e.g., ./src/file.py)

pattern__traversal.title: Traversal
pattern__traversal.description: Parent directory traversal — any path containing ".." is a violation regardless of whether it resolves to a safe location.

pattern__env.title: Env
pattern__env.description: .env files and directories at any depth. Secrets must never be accessible to agents.

pattern__home.title: Home
pattern__home.description: Home directory in isolation — granting ~/ or its expanded form gives access to the entire home tree. Always a security violation.

pattern__root.title: Root
pattern__root.description: Filesystem root in isolation — granting / gives access to the entire filesystem. Always a security violation.

pattern__claude.title: Claude

pattern__absolute.title: Absolute

atom__path_relative.description: Relative filesystem path starting with ./ — excludes traversal and sensitive path patterns. Workspace-relative, gets absolutized during resolution.

atom__path_absolute.title: PathAbsolute
atom__path_absolute.description: Absolute filesystem path starting with / — excludes traversal and sensitive path patterns. The resolved form after absolutization.

union__path_any.title: PathAny
union__path_any.description: Filesystem path — either relative (./) or absolute (/)

enum__capabilities.title: Capabilities
enum__capabilities.description: Platform-agnostic capability descriptor. Format transformers map these to vendor-specific tools. read: file read. search: find files by name or content. write: create or overwrite files. edit: targeted modification. append: add content to end of files. inspect: read-only command execution.

atom__kebab_string.title: KebabString
atom__kebab_string.description: Lowercase kebab-case string — words separated by hyphens. Used for identifiers that must be URL-safe and filesystem-safe.

simplegroup__context_item_raw.title: ContextItem
simplegroup__context_item_raw.description: A label+path pair for a context resource — auto-derives read permission

context_label.title: ContextLabel
context_label.description:
Display label for a context resource. Used in the generated prompt to create readable section headers. "Output Schema", "Canonical Glossary", "Operations Guide". Keep concise — this appears in the agent's prompt.
Title Case string — each word starts uppercase, separated by spaces. Used for display titles, section headings, and short labels. Not prose (no sentences), not an identifier (has spaces).

checks: Descriptive enough to identify the resource without seeing its content
Concise — a label, not a sentence

context_path.description:

Whether the resource is mandatory or merely offered is carried by the array this item sits in — context_required or context_available — never by the path itself.
